newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico industry group wants tortilla price free-up.
newsitem.headline: Mexico industry group wants tortilla price free-up.

text.p: Mexico's Confederation of Industrial Chambers (Concamin) said Tuesday it wants price controls on corn-pancake tortillas to be lifted so the sector can become part of the free market.
"This industry will continue going downhill (if price controls are not lifted) and we are going to keep having problems of tortilla shortages...," Concamin Chairman Victor Diaz Romero told reporters.
Tortillas, eaten more widely than bread, are one of a handful of foodstuffs with prices controlled by the government to make sure poor people have access to basic food.
Private sector groups such as Concamin, the umbrella group for the country's industrial chambers, have long been pushing for price freedom for tortillas.
But the Trade Ministry, fearing a spike in inflation, has so far declined to liberate prices, prefering to award occasional increase in prices.
Tortilla makers are demanding prices rise to 2.50 pesos per kilo from the current 1.75 pesos.
